blocks.prompt: 22 Solve the initial value problem \(\frac{dy}{dx} - x = xy^2\); \(y(0) = 1\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh initial value problem (IVP) hai, yani equation ke saath ek shart (condition) bhi di hui hai: \(x = 0\) par \(y = 1\).
Is ka matlab hai do kaam: pehle general solution nikalna, phir condition se constant \(C\) ki asal value maloom karna.
Diya kya hai? \(\frac{dy}{dx} - x = xy^2\) aur \(y(0) = 1\). Find kya karna hai? Particular solution.
Rule kaunsa? \(x\) common nikalne se \(\frac{dy}{dx} = x(1 + y^2)\) banta hai, jo separable hai.
Plan: factorise, variables alag, integrate (\(\tan^{-1}\) aayega), phir condition lagana.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{dy}{dx} - x = xy^2\), \(y(0) = 1\).
Maloom karna: particular solution.
Tareeqa: Separable equation ka general solution, phir initial value condition \(y(x_0) = y_0\) (Section 4.2) se \(C\) nikalna.

Factorise karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x + xy^2 = x(1 + y^2)\]
Kyun: \(-x\) ko right side le gaye aur \(x\) common nikala. Ab right side \(x\) ka hissa times \(y\) ka hissa hai, jo separable ki pehchaan hai.

Variables alag karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{1 + y^2} = x\,dx\]
Kyun: \(1 + y^2\) se divide kiya; yeh kabhi zero nahi hota, is liye koi solution zaaya nahi hua.

Integrate karein
\[\tan^{-1} y = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + C\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{1 + y^2}\) ka integral \(\tan^{-1} y\) hai aur \(x\) ka \(\frac{x^2}{2}\). Yeh general solution hai, abhi \(C\) koi bhi ho sakta hai.

\(y(0) = 1\) lagayein
\[\tan^{-1} 1 = 0 + C\]
\[C = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
Kyun: General solution mein \(x = 0\) aur \(y = 1\) rakha. \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\), is liye \(\tan^{-1} 1 = \frac{\pi}{4}\).
Dhyan dein: Condition hamesha integrate karne ke baad lagti hai, pehle nahi; aur \(\tan^{-1} 1\) ko \(45\) likhne ki bajaye radians mein \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) likhein.

Particular solution
\[\tan^{-1} y = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
\[y = \tan\left(\dfrac{x^2}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\]
Kyun: Dono taraf \(\tan\) lene se \(y\) akela ho gaya; dono shaklein sahi jawab hain.

Tasdeeq
\[y' = x\sec^2\left(\tfrac{x^2}{2} + \tfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\]
\[= x(1 + y^2)\]
is liye \(y' - x = xy^2\) \(\checkmark\); aur \(y(0) = \tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\) \(\checkmark\)
Kyun: Chain rule se andar wale \(\frac{x^2}{2}\) ka derivative \(x\) bahar aaya, aur identity \(\sec^2\theta = 1 + \tan^2\theta\) lagayi.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein is sawal ka jawab number 25 par chhapa hai, 22 par nahi. Exercise 4.2 ki keys 2 se 29 tak hain jabke sawal sirf 25 hain (key 2 Question 1 ka jawab hai, aur keys 15, 19 aur 27 kisi chhape hue sawal ki nahi), is liye jawab 25 par dhoondiye, warna aap kisi aur sawal ka jawab dekh kar pareshan ho jayenge. Jawab khud, \(\tan^{-1} y = \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{\pi}{4}\), sahi hai.
